newsitem.title: USA: U.S. companies unconcerned by dollar's rise - NYT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. companies unconcerned by dollar's rise - NYT.

text.p: The number of U.S. companies expressing concern over the rise of the dollar has been surprisingly small, the New York Times said Wednesday.
In recent days officials at Boeing Co, General Electric Co and Intel Corp have dismissed worries about the dollar, the paper reported.
The paper said many U.S. companies have insulated themselves from the dollar's effects by expanding production overseas, aggressive cost-cutting and active hedging of securities.
"We can export our machines to Japan and Europe with a landed cost that is competitive, even at the current exchange rates," Gleason Corp Chairman James Gleason told the paper.

The paper said Gleason cited a number of reasons -- which were echoed by other executives -- for why the rising dollar had done little harm: cost cutting over the last decade, abstention from significant price increases and expansion of overseas production.
